key_insight: The paper replaces the usual special-quasirandom-structure plus ideal-entropy approximation with an energy-cumulant expansion that captures short-range order and improves free-energy predictions for disordered phases.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical route to screen phase stability, order-disorder behavior, and defect/cluster populations in complex alloys and oxides without expensive Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics.
method: Express the disordered-phase free energy as an infinite expansion in energy cumulants.
Estimate higher-order cumulants from energies of random atomic arrangements instead of sampling full finite-temperature trajectories.
Use the expansion to compute phase diagrams, defect concentrations, and short-range order, then apply it with a foundation interatomic potential to screen lithium-excess rocksalt oxides.
evidence_signal: In a nine-element refractory system, including the second cumulant reduced free-energy errors by about an order of magnitude, and the method was used to screen 26-element composition space for synthesizable disordered Li-rich phases.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on having representative random-configuration energies and a reliable underlying potential, so poor training data or insufficient sampling could degrade the cumulant estimates.
paper_title: Beyond special quasirandom structures: free energies from energy cumulants
